title: Project Appraisal Level 3: Advanced Project Risk, Structuring and Monitoring
subtitle: Stress-test projects, structure large and complex financing, and steer loans through construction and trouble
summary: For senior analysts and committee members: measure how much risk a project really carries, design a financing and security package that allocates it sensibly, and manage the loan through construction, start-up and distress.
audience: Senior credit and project analysts, relationship managers for corporate and project loans, and credit committee members. Entry: Project Appraisal Level 2, or Credit Level 3 with project experience.
objectives: Run sensitivity, switching value and scenario analysis, and read their effect on NPV and DSCR
Assess economic, environmental, social, foreign exchange and regulatory risks
Structure large projects with syndication, co-financing, supplier credit, leasing, sponsor support and reserve accounts
Monitor implementation and operation, spot cost overruns and delays, and restructure troubled project loans
Lead a committee through a complex project decision

runningCase.name: Sebeta Pasta and Flour PLC
runningCase.text: A fictional pasta and flour plant from Levels 1 and 2: a Birr 100.1 million project with a Birr 70 million loan at 16% and sculpted repayment (Birr 7 million in year 2, then Birr 9 million a year). Base NPV at 16% is Birr 19.6 million, IRR 20.6% and minimum DSCR 1.31. In this course you stress-test it, build its support and security package, follow it through a one-year delay and overrun, and decide on a pasta line expansion two years after rescheduling.

modules.title: Risk analysis: sensitivity, switching values and scenarios
modules.summary: Find the few assumptions that decide a project's fate and measure how little they need to move before the project, or the loan, fails.
objectives: Run one-at-a-time sensitivity tests and read their effect on NPV, IRR and minimum DSCR
Calculate a switching value and use it to rank critical assumptions
Build a plausible downside scenario and test whether the loan survives it
Prepare a risk matrix that names the mitigant and the risk bearer for each risk
Judge when probabilistic (Monte Carlo) analysis adds value

lessons.title: The base case is only one guess
body: Every project appraisal rests on a base case: one set of prices, volumes, costs and dates. At Level 2 the Sebeta Pasta and Flour PLC model gave an NPV at 16% of Birr 19.6 million, an IRR of 20.6% and a minimum DSCR of 1.31. Those numbers are only as good as the assumptions behind them.

Risk analysis asks a sharper question: which assumptions would you bet your job on, and which ones, if wrong, would sink the project or the loan? In most Ethiopian manufacturing projects the answer is a short list: selling price, the cost of the main raw material, capacity utilization, investment cost and the start-up date.
A senior analyst spends most of the due diligence effort on those few assumptions, not evenly across the whole spreadsheet.

items.label: Selling price
items.text: Birr 6,000 a tonne in Sebeta's base case

items.label: Volume and utilization
items.text: 60%, 75%, then 85% of capacity

items.label: Variable cost
items.text: Mainly wheat, much of it imported

items.label: Investment cost
items.text: Building and machinery overruns

items.label: Delay
items.text: Late start-up pushes revenue back a year

example.title: Sebeta warm-up: which assumption would you bet your job on?
example.text: At Bank A's training day, analyst Meron Alemu said she would bet her job on the building cost, because a fixed-price contract was signed with Abebe Construction PLC. Her colleague Dawit Gebre said he would bet on nothing linked to wheat, because Sebeta imports most of its wheat and the price moves with world markets and the exchange rate. The sensitivity results later showed Dawit was right to worry: price and wheat cost, not construction, decide Sebeta's fate.

lessons.tip: Before running any test, write down the three assumptions you trust least. Then check whether the numbers agree with your instinct.

lessons.title: Sensitivity analysis: one assumption at a time
body: Sensitivity analysis changes one assumption at a time while holding all others at the base case, and records NPV, IRR and minimum DSCR after each change. Typical tests are price down 10%, variable costs up 10%, investment cost up 15% and a one-year delay in start-up.

The size of the change matters less than consistency: use the same tests across projects so the credit committee can compare them. Then read the results as a ranking. The test that moves NPV the most points to the assumption that needs the strongest evidence.

visual.caption: Sebeta's IRR under one-at-a-time changes. The project's cost of capital is 16%.

worked.title: Sebeta sensitivity results (NPV at 16%, Birr million)

rows.label: Investment cost +10.5 (15% overrun on building and machinery)

worked.note: A 10% fall in price wipes out Birr 48.6 million of value, almost five times the damage of a 15% cost overrun. Price is the critical assumption.

lessons.title: Switching values: how far before the project fails
body: A switching value is the change in one assumption that brings NPV to zero, or brings DSCR down to the bank's floor. It turns a sensitivity table into a single, powerful message: "the project fails if price falls by more than 4.1%".

If NPV changes roughly in a straight line, the switching value is the base NPV divided by the change in NPV for each 1% move. A small switching value marks a critical assumption. It needs the strongest market evidence, and usually a contract or structural mitigant, before the bank lends.

worked.title: Sebeta switching values

rows.label: Investment overrun
rows.value: about Birr 20 million (about 29% of building and machinery)

rows.label: Ranking
rows.value: Price, then variable cost (wheat), then investment cost

worked.note: Price and wheat cost are critical because the contribution margin is only 38%. A cost overrun is a lesser threat.

scenario.title: Where to spend the due diligence budget
scenario.situation: You have two weeks and one market consultant's day to firm up Sebeta's appraisal. The sponsor's file is thick on construction quotations and thin on pasta price history. The switching values are price -4.1%, variable cost +6.6% and investment overrun about 29%.
scenario.question: Where should the consultant's day go?
options: Re-checking the building quotations, since construction is the largest cash outlay
Pasta and flour price history and the wheat cost outlook
Reviewing the machinery supplier's catalogue
Spreading it evenly across all assumptions
scenario.explain: The smallest switching values (price and wheat cost) mark the assumptions that can sink the project, so they deserve the scarce expert time. Construction cost could rise by about 29% before NPV reaches zero.

lessons.title: Scenario analysis: risks move together
body: In real life assumptions do not move one at a time. A weak market year brings lower prices and slower ramp-up together. Scenario analysis moves several assumptions in one plausible story, and asks whether the loan survives a realistic downside, not only the base case.

For the bank the key output is DSCR year by year, not only NPV. Sebeta's sculpted repayment (Birr 7 million in year 2, then Birr 9 million a year) gives a minimum base DSCR of 1.31, but a downside of 55/65/80% utilization with price down 5% drops DSCR below 1.0 in years 1 and 2, and project NPV to -16.1.
A DSCR below 1.0 in the downside does not automatically mean decline. It tells the bank how much cash support it needs in place before the shortfall happens.

worked.title: Sebeta DSCR under stress (sculpted structure)
worked.note: In the downside the bank is not paid in full from operating cash in years 1 and 2. The real risk is margin (pasta price versus wheat cost), not construction cost.

regulation.source: A typical Ethiopian bank credit manual (2025), tenure and grace
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual allows grace of up to 24 months on long-term loans, set on the projected cash flow and applied to principal only; interest may still be payable during grace. Long-term loans are typically capped at 10 years excluding grace. Stress results should therefore be read against the grace and tenor the policy actually allows.

scenario.title: The downside DSCR is 0.68
scenario.situation: Sebeta's downside scenario shows DSCR of 0.68 in year 1 and 0.75 in year 2, recovering to 1.09 in year 3 and 1.24 in year 5. The sponsors, Tsegaye and Almaz Worku, have strong other businesses and Birr 26.1 million of equity already committed.
scenario.question: What is the best credit response?
options: Decline: any DSCR below 1.0 is unacceptable
Approve as proposed; the base case is what matters
Halve the loan and let the sponsors find the rest elsewhere
Approve subject to a sponsor-funded DSRA, a shortfall undertaking until DSCR reaches 1.25 for two years, and wheat supply contracts with price formulas
scenario.explain: The downside shortfall is temporary and the project recovers, so the right answer is to put cash support in place before it happens. Declining ignores the recovery; approving unchanged leaves the bank exposed in years 1 and 2.

lessons.title: The risk matrix: who carries each risk
body: A risk matrix lists each risk, its likelihood, its impact, the mitigant, and who bears it: the sponsor, the contractor, the supplier, the insurer or the bank. It turns the analysis into a structuring tool: every serious risk should end up with the party best able to control or absorb it.
If the last column says "bank" for a high-likelihood, high-impact risk, the structure is not finished. Either a mitigant moves the risk to someone else, or the loan amount and price must reflect it.

items.label: Name the risk
items.text: For example, wheat price rises faster than pasta prices

items.label: Rate likelihood
items.text: Low, medium or high, with evidence

items.label: Rate impact
items.text: Use the sensitivity and switching values

items.label: Choose the mitigant
items.text: Contract, reserve, insurance, equity or covenant

items.label: Assign the risk bearer
items.text: Sponsor, contractor, supplier, insurer or bank

points: Construction overrun: medium likelihood, moderate impact; fixed-price contract and sponsor overrun undertaking; borne by contractor and sponsors
Margin squeeze: medium likelihood, high impact; supply contracts with price formulas and a DSRA; borne by sponsors and suppliers
Fire or machinery breakdown: low likelihood, high impact; insurance with the bank as first beneficiary; borne by the insurer

example.title: Kality Steel Pipes: a risk matrix that changed the loan
example.text: When Bank A appraised a Birr 45 million pipe plant for Kality Steel Pipes PLC, the analyst's matrix showed that steel coil prices (high likelihood, high impact) were borne entirely by the bank, because the sponsor had no supply contract. The committee asked for a twelve-month coil supply agreement and an extra Birr 5 million of equity before approval. The sponsor agreed, and the matrix's last column changed from "bank" to "sponsor and supplier".

lessons.title: Probabilistic analysis and the Hawassa Dairy case
body: Probabilistic analysis (Monte Carlo) gives each key assumption a range and a probability, runs thousands of combinations and reports the probability that NPV is negative. It is useful for very large projects with good data, but it is no substitute for judgment on the key assumptions: a model fed with guesses produces precise-looking guesses.
The Hawassa Dairy case from Level 2 shows the opposite problem: a project so thin that every single test destroys its value. Base NPV at 16% is only Birr 1.6 million and IRR 17.2%.

worked.title: How fragile is Hawassa Dairy? (NPV at 16%, Birr million)

rows.label: Price -5% with unchanged cost per litre

worked.note: Every single change makes NPV negative. The dairy has almost no margin for error.

example.title: Hawassa Dairy's mitigants
example.text: The teams proposed signed milk supply contracts with a price formula linked to selling prices, offtake agreements with the sponsor's supermarkets and institutions, more equity, and a slower, smaller first phase. Facilitator Hirut Bekele reminded them that without these the bank should decline or reduce the loan, however attractive the sponsor.

scenario.title: Hawassa Dairy at committee
scenario.situation: The sponsor of Hawassa Dairy offers no milk supply contracts and no offtake agreements, but proposes collateral worth 120% of the loan. Each sensitivity test turns NPV negative.
scenario.question: What should the analyst recommend?
options: Approve, because collateral covers the loan
Approve with a higher interest rate to price the risk
Decline or reduce the loan unless supply contracts, offtake agreements or more equity are provided
Ask for a Monte Carlo study before deciding
scenario.explain: Collateral is a second way out, not a reason to finance a project that cannot repay from its own cash. A higher rate makes the thin margin worse, and Monte Carlo cannot fix the missing contracts.

takeaways: Sensitivity changes one assumption at a time; scenarios move several together in a plausible story.
A switching value is the change that brings NPV to zero or DSCR to the floor; the smaller it is, the more critical the assumption.
For Sebeta the real risk is margin: price (-4.1%) and wheat cost (+6.6%), not construction cost (about 29%).
A downside DSCR below 1.0 calls for cash support (DSRA, sponsor undertaking, supply contracts), not automatic decline.
Every risk in the matrix needs a mitigant and a named risk bearer; "bank" in the last column for a big risk means the structure is unfinished.

quiz.q: What is a switching value?
options: The interest rate at which NPV is highest
The difference between IRR and the cost of capital
The change in one assumption that brings NPV to zero or DSCR to the bank's floor
The price at which the sponsor agrees to sell
quiz.explain: It shows how far an assumption can move before the project or the loan fails.

quiz.q: Why is scenario analysis needed in addition to sensitivity analysis?
options: Risks move together in real life, so one-at-a-time tests understate a combined downside
It replaces the base case
It is required only for export projects
It always gives a higher NPV
quiz.explain: A weak market year usually brings lower prices and slower ramp-up together.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a column of a risk matrix?
options: Likelihood
Mitigant
Risk bearer
The analyst's salary grade
quiz.explain: The usual columns are risk, likelihood, impact, mitigant and risk bearer.

quiz.q: Which Sebeta assumption is most critical?
options: Building cost, because it is the largest outlay
Selling price, with the smallest switching value of about -4.1%
The interest rate on the loan
Staff numbers
quiz.explain: With a contribution margin of only 38%, a small price fall wipes out NPV.

quiz.q: Sebeta's NPV is 19.6 and falls by 4.8 for each 1% fall in price. What is the price switching value?
options: About 4.1%
About 2.4%
About 9.4%
About 24%

quiz.q: Which pair are both mitigants for weak early-year DSCR?
options: Faster repayment and lower equity
A higher interest rate and a shorter tenor
A longer grace period and a debt service reserve account
Removing insurance and cutting the DSRA
quiz.explain: Longer grace, sculpted repayment, a DSRA, a sponsor shortfall undertaking and more equity all help.

modules.title: Economic, environmental, social and regulatory appraisal
modules.summary: Look beyond the project's own profit and loss to the risks that can close a profitable plant: pollution, community conflict, foreign exchange and changing regulation.
objectives: Explain how economic appraisal differs from financial appraisal
Measure a project's foreign exchange earning or saving
Apply the environmental and social checks a bank requires for large project loans
Identify foreign exchange, incentive and regulatory dependencies and set conditions for them

lessons.title: Economic appraisal: good for the country, not only the owners
body: Financial appraisal asks whether the project pays its owners and lenders. Economic appraisal asks whether it benefits the economy: foreign exchange earned or saved, jobs created, use of local inputs, links to farmers and suppliers, and whether it survives only because of protection or subsidies.

Formal economic appraisal uses shadow prices (for example a shadow exchange rate) instead of market prices, removes taxes and subsidies as transfers, and counts external costs and benefits such as pollution or training. Banks rarely run a full economic model, but they use the questions to set priorities: many Ethiopian banks give priority to activities that earn or save foreign exchange and encourage exporters and importers of essential goods.

left.title: Financial appraisal
items: Taxes and subsidies counted as cash
Only the project's own cash flows
Question: can it repay and earn a return?

right.title: Economic appraisal
items: Shadow prices, for example for foreign exchange
Taxes and subsidies treated as transfers

example.title: A protected juice plant
example.text: Ziway Fruit Processing PLC showed a healthy financial IRR, but only because imported juice faced high duties and its sugar came at a subsidized price. Analyst Kebede Haile noted that if protection were reduced the plant would lose its margin. The committee approved a smaller first phase and asked for a plan to cut costs, treating the dependence on protection as a regulatory risk.

lessons.title: Sebeta's economic and foreign exchange profile
body: Sebeta replaces imported pasta but needs imported wheat, so its foreign exchange effect is a net figure. The plant needs about 17,000 tonnes of imported wheat a year, about USD 5.1 million at USD 300 a tonne, and replaces an estimated 8,000 tonnes of imported pasta worth about USD 7.2 million.

The net saving of about USD 2.1 million a year is a genuine economic benefit, but it does not remove the project's own exposure: every tonne of wheat still needs foreign exchange at the right time. The bank's response is to require a foreign exchange plan and to encourage local wheat contracts with cooperatives.

worked.title: Sebeta's net foreign exchange effect

rows.label: Jobs
rows.value: about 180, plus purchases from local wheat cooperatives

worked.note: Positive for the economy, but still exposed to foreign exchange availability for wheat. Condition: a foreign exchange plan and local wheat supply contracts.

items.label: Foreign exchange
items.text: Net saving about USD 2.1 m a year; plan required

items.label: Jobs and linkages
items.text: About 180 jobs; local cooperatives supply wheat

items.label: Environment
items.text: Flour dust, noise and pasta-line wastewater

items.label: Social
items.text: Leased industrial land, no resettlement

items.label: Regulatory
items.text: Flour prices have at times faced government intervention

lessons.title: Environmental and social appraisal
body: A profitable plant can be closed by a regulator or a community. For large project loans a typical Ethiopian bank manual requires the analyst to assess legislation that could hurt operations, the project's impact on the natural environment with a clear waste disposal method, and management's capacity to control the process from raw material to waste.

In practice the analyst checks for an approved environmental impact assessment under national law, land acquisition and compensation, community consultation, worker health and safety, and water use. For Sebeta that means dust extraction and fire systems in the investment cost, wastewater treatment for the pasta line, and EIA approval as a condition precedent to disbursement.

regulation.source: Environmental Impact Assessment Proclamation No. 299/2002 and Environmental Pollution Control Proclamation No. 300/2002; A typical Ethiopian bank credit manual (2025), environmental analysis
regulation.text: Ethiopian law requires environmental impact assessment for projects likely to have significant impacts, and controls pollution and waste discharge. A typical Ethiopian bank manual adds that before deciding a big project loan, the bank must assess current legislation that could harm operations, the project's impact on the environment including its waste disposal mechanism, and management's capacity to control the process from inputs to waste.

items.label: EIA approval
items.text: From the competent environmental authority

items.label: Impacts and mitigation
items.text: Main impacts, measures and their cost in the budget

items.label: Land and community
items.text: Lease, compensation, consultation, no unresolved claims

items.label: Health and safety
items.text: Dust, fire, noise, chemicals

items.label: Monitoring plan
items.text: Who measures what, how often, reported to the bank

scenario.title: Dust filters missing from the budget
scenario.situation: Selam Tesfaye reviews the cost breakdown for a Birr 60 million flour mill at Bishoftu. The EIA report lists dust extraction as a required mitigation, but the investment budget has no line for it. The sponsor says the filters can be added later from profits.
scenario.question: What should Selam do?
options: Add the cost of the dust system to the project budget and financing plan, and make it a condition before the related disbursement
Accept the sponsor's promise and proceed
Decline the loan outright
Ignore it, since environmental matters are for the regulator
scenario.explain: Mitigation must be costed and financed up front; a missing safety system is both an environmental breach and an explosion risk to the bank's security. Declining is excessive when the fix is clear.

lessons.title: Foreign exchange and regulatory risk
body: Imported machinery and raw materials need foreign exchange. Delays in allocation delay construction and production, so foreign exchange is a project risk even for a company that sells only in Birr. The appraisal should show where each dollar comes from: retention balances, purchases from the bank, supplier credit or franco valuta.

Licences, land lease terms, price controls and tax incentives can also change. The analyst lists which ones the project depends on, and builds the important ones into the downside scenario. Sebeta's flour prices, for example, have at times been subject to government intervention.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/01/2024 (Foreign Exchange Directive), as amended including FXD/04/2026
regulation.text: Since July 29, 2024 banks buy and sell foreign currency at freely negotiated rates. Exporters must repatriate proceeds within three months, convert 50% to Birr and may keep 50% in a retention account. The February 2026 amendment (FXD/04/2026) lets banks approve external loans and supplier credits without prior NBE approval, with monthly reporting. A credit manual written earlier may still say supplier credit needs prior written NBE approval, so check the directive in force on the day.

points: Supplier credit for exporters: repayment from export proceeds only, under a typical bank manual
Export projects may be eligible for an export credit guarantee scheme that covers part of the loss if the borrower defaults, subject to its eligibility rules
Price controls, land lease renewals and duty incentives: note each dependency and its expiry date

example.title: Machinery stuck for want of dollars
example.text: Adama Packaging PLC had its building finished on time, but its Birr 22 million of imported machinery waited five months because the foreign exchange plan assumed purchases that were not available when needed. Interest kept running during the idle months. Bank A now asks every importing project for a month-by-month foreign exchange plan with named sources before the first disbursement.

lessons.title: Duty-free collateral and export guarantees
body: Investment incentives affect security as well as cash flow. A typical Ethiopian bank manual values duty-free vehicles and machinery net of the duty (or including duty only if payment is confirmed), and accepts them only as security for the privileged owner's own loans in the same sector, never for third-party loans.

An export credit guarantee covers part of the loss if an exporter defaults. It is useful, but it does not remove the need for appraisal: it has its own eligibility rules, it covers only part of the loss, and a claim can fail if its conditions were not met.

regulation.source: A typical Ethiopian bank credit manual (2025), collateral and insurance chapters
regulation.text: Duty-free vehicles and machinery are valued net of the duty free amount, or including duty if payment is ascertained, and are accepted only for the same sector and the same owner holding the privilege. The duty amount must be shown in the insurance policy.

scenario.title: The guarantee as a reason to relax collateral
scenario.situation: Hailu Leather Exports PLC holds an export credit guarantee covering part of any loss on a pre-shipment facility. The sponsor asks Bank A to waive the building mortgage it normally requires, "since the guarantee already protects you".
scenario.question: How should the bank respond?
options: Waive all collateral, because the guarantee is enough
Refuse to accept the guarantee at all
Keep normal credit analysis and collateral, and check that the guarantee's own conditions are met
Double the interest rate instead of taking collateral
scenario.explain: The guarantee covers only part of the loss and has its own eligibility rules, so it complements, not replaces, sound analysis and security.

lessons.title: Case study: the Modjo tannery expansion
body: A leather tannery in Modjo asks for Birr 150 million to double capacity. It exports finished leather and earns about USD 6 million a year through the bank. The existing plant discharges partly treated effluent containing chromium into a nearby river; residents have complained to the regional environmental authority, which has issued a warning letter. The expansion budget includes no new effluent treatment plant.

The risks go far beyond the new loan: regulatory closure of the whole plant would stop repayment on existing and new loans. Add legal liability and clean-up costs, reputational risk for the bank, community conflict, and export buyers who increasingly demand environmental certification.

worked.title: Making the Modjo expansion financeable: conditions

rows.label: Project cost
rows.value: Add a modern effluent treatment plant to the budget

rows.label: Independent check
rows.value: Environmental audit by a qualified firm

rows.label: Covenants
rows.value: Discharge monitoring, reported to the bank

rows.label: Export guarantee
rows.value: Treated as partial loss cover only, its own conditions met

worked.note: As designed, the expansion should not be financed. With these conditions it can be reconsidered on its merits.

example.title: Why a warning letter matters
example.text: Relationship manager Tigist Mekonnen pointed out to her committee that the warning letter put the bank's existing Birr 80 million exposure to the tannery at risk, not only the new request. Closing the plant for even three months would stop export earnings and the repayments that depend on them.

scenario.title: The Modjo request as designed
scenario.situation: The tannery's expansion is profitable on paper and the sponsor is a long-standing exporter. The budget has no effluent treatment plant and the regional authority has issued a warning letter.
scenario.question: What is the right decision on the request as submitted?
options: Approve, given the strong export record
Do not finance as designed; reconsider only with an effluent plant in the cost, authority approval before disbursement, an independent audit and monitoring covenants
Approve, but add a covenant to treat effluent within five years
Approve half the amount now and the rest after the complaint is resolved
scenario.explain: Regulatory closure would stop repayment on every loan to the tannery, so the environmental fix must be built in before any money moves.

takeaways: Economic appraisal asks whether the country gains: foreign exchange, jobs, local inputs, linkages and survival without protection.
Foreign exchange is a project risk even for a domestic seller; require a month-by-month foreign exchange plan.
For big projects, assess legislation, environmental impact and waste disposal, and management's control capacity; make EIA approval a condition precedent.
Duty-free assets are valued net of duty and secure only the privileged owner's own loans in the same sector.
An export credit guarantee covers part of a loss; it never replaces appraisal or collateral.

quiz.q: Which question belongs to economic rather than financial appraisal?
options: Does the project earn or save foreign exchange for the country?
What is the loan's repayment schedule?
What is the sponsor's equity contribution?
What interest rate will the bank charge?
quiz.explain: Economic appraisal looks at foreign exchange, jobs, local inputs, linkages and dependence on protection.

quiz.q: Which three items does a typical Ethiopian bank manual require in the environmental assessment of big projects?
options: Profit, tax and dividends
Legislation that could harm operations; impact on the environment and waste disposal; management's capacity to control the process
Staff numbers, salaries and pensions
Collateral value, insurance and guarantees
quiz.explain: These three issues must be assessed before deciding a big project loan.

quiz.q: Why is foreign exchange allocation a project risk even for a domestic seller?
options: Domestic sales are paid in dollars
Banks charge more interest to domestic sellers
Imported machinery or inputs need foreign exchange, and delays stop construction or production
It is not a risk for domestic sellers
quiz.explain: Sebeta sells in Birr but needs about USD 5.1 million of wheat a year.

quiz.q: What restriction applies to duty-free machinery offered as collateral?
options: It is valued net of duty and accepted only for the privileged owner's own loans in the same sector
It can secure any borrower's loan
None; it is valued at full invoice price
It must be sold before the loan is approved
quiz.explain: Duty-free assets cannot secure third-party loans.

quiz.q: Does an export credit guarantee remove the need for appraisal?
options: Yes, the guarantor carries all the risk
Only for coffee exporters
Yes, if the exporter has traded for one year
No; it covers part of the loss and has its own eligibility rules
quiz.explain: Normal credit analysis and security still apply.

quiz.q: Under FXD/01/2024, what must exporters do with their proceeds?
options: Keep 100% abroad
Repatriate within three months, convert 50% to Birr and may keep 50% in a retention account
Convert all proceeds to Birr on the day of shipment
Repatriate within one year
quiz.explain: This is the rule in the Foreign Exchange Directive as summarized in the NBE directives list.

modules.title: Complex financing structures and the security package
modules.summary: Finance projects too large or too risky for a simple loan by sharing exposure with other lenders and placing each risk on the party best able to carry it.
objectives: Size the bank's share of a large project against the large-exposure limit and board appetite
Explain the roles and rights of lead, agent and participant banks in a syndication
Choose among co-financing, supplier credit, leasing and loan buyout
Design sponsor support, reserve accounts and a security package that allocate risk sensibly

lessons.title: Why and how banks syndicate
body: A syndicated loan is shared among two or more banks because of its size and risk, usually medium to long term for large investments. A bank may act as lead, joint lead or participant. Many Ethiopian banks prefer to lead: the loan contract is then signed between the lead bank and the borrower, and the lead bank collects all repayments.

As a participant, the bank should insist on the right to review the loan contract, do its own independent analysis, inspect the loan administration and receive regular status reports. It should weigh the loan amount, its own and the lead bank's liquidity, the nature of the project, its share, the collateral, the risks and the lead bank's experience.

regulation.text: A bank's exposure to one counterparty group may not exceed 25% of its total capital; any exposure of 10% or more of total capital is a large exposure and is reported to the NBE monthly within 20 days. Projects larger than one bank can carry are therefore shared through syndication.

left.title: Our bank as lead
items: Negotiates terms and signs with the borrower
Collects repayments and gives participants quarterly follow-up reports

right.title: Our bank as participant
items: Receives periodic reports and pays an administration fee to the lead

lessons.title: The participation agreement and the agent bank
body: A loan participation (co-financing) agreement binds all lenders. It sets each bank's share and pro rata rights, the lead bank's duties (documentation, disbursement, collection, reporting), shared security, voting, events of default and enforcement, and fees. Rescheduling, extension or any other amendment of the loan contract needs the consent of all lenders.

An agent bank checks that disbursement, repayment and grace follow the agreement, computes and collects interest and principal and distributes it, monitors collateral, guarantees, insurance and covenants, and collects periodic reports from the borrower.

regulation.source: A typical Ethiopian bank credit manual (2025), syndicated loans
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires a separate loan participation agreement among all participating banks, makes rescheduling, extension or any other amendment subject to the consent of all lenders, has the lead bank provide participants with quarterly loan administration, project follow-up and visit reports, and reserves approval of all syndicated loans for its highest management credit committee.

items.label: Mandate and feasibility
items.text: Lead studies the project

items.label: Invite participants
items.text: Syndication proposal with pricing, terms and fees

items.label: Sign agreements
items.text: Participation agreement among banks, loan contract with borrower

items.label: Register security
items.text: Held for all lenders pro rata

items.label: Disburse and administer
items.text: Agent collects and distributes; quarterly reports

scenario.title: A participant's must-have rights
scenario.situation: Bank A is invited to take Birr 300 million of a Birr 1,200 million syndicated loan for Gelan Glass Factory PLC. The lead bank's draft agreement lets the lead amend repayment terms alone "to save time", and offers participants an annual summary report.
scenario.question: Which change should Bank A insist on first?
options: A higher arrangement fee
Permission to sell its share without telling anyone
A seat on the borrower's board
Unanimous consent for rescheduling and amendments, plus regular (quarterly) follow-up reports and the right to review the contract and inspect administration
scenario.explain: Without consent rights and regular information, a participant carries the risk with no control over it. Fees matter less than protection.

lessons.title: Co-financing, supplier credit, leasing and loan buyout
body: Not every gap needs another commercial bank. Development lenders co-finance priority projects. Foreign suppliers sometimes offer deferred payment for machinery and inputs. Leasing companies can buy equipment and lease it to the project. A bank can also buy out or take over a loan from another bank to gain first-degree security or a good customer.

Each source brings its own rules. Supplier credit for exporters is repaid from export proceeds only. Leasing moves ownership of the asset to the lessor, which changes the security package. A loan takeover requires the other bank's undertaking to release documents and confirmation that the loan is in pass status.

items.label: Co-financing
items.text: Development lenders share the project on agreed terms

items.label: Supplier credit
items.text: Deferred payment from the foreign supplier, repaid from export proceeds

items.label: Equipment leasing
items.text: One bank procedure: term loans to lessors up to 10 years with at least 40% equity

items.label: Loan buyout
items.text: Take over another bank's pass-status loan and first-degree security

example.title: Supplier credit for a sesame hulling line
example.text: Humera Agro Exports PLC imported a USD 1.4 million hulling line on 18-month supplier credit. Bank A opened the import letter of credit, took full collateral and set a covenant that export proceeds would pass through the bank. When the first instalment fell due, the export retention account covered it, exactly as the structure intended.

lessons.title: Sponsor support and reserve accounts
body: Sponsor support keeps construction and early operating risk with the people who control the project. A completion guarantee covers the loan until the plant is completed and passes a defined test. A cost overrun undertaking makes sponsors fund any overrun with equity, not bank debt. A debt service shortfall undertaking covers shortfalls until DSCR is above the floor for an agreed period.

Reserve accounts hold cash for bad times. A debt service reserve account (DSRA) holds cash equal to, for example, six months of debt service, blocked and used only if cash flow falls short. One bank procedure also requires interest for the grace period to be deposited in a blocked account in advance.

items.label: Completion guarantee
items.text: Until the plant passes its completion test

items.label: Cost overrun undertaking
items.text: Overruns funded by sponsor equity

items.label: Shortfall undertaking
items.text: Until DSCR stays above the floor

items.label: DSRA
items.text: For example 6 months of debt service, blocked

items.label: Interest during grace deposit
items.text: Grace-period interest deposited in advance

worked.title: Sizing Sebeta's DSRA (illustrative)

rows.label: Interest at 16% on about Birr 63 million outstanding
Range used in the package
rows.value: Birr 8 to 10 million, funded before first repayment

worked.note: The DSRA would have covered most of the downside shortfall in years 1 and 2, buying time for the recovery shown in year 3.

lessons.title: Building the security package
body: A project security package typically includes a mortgage over the land lease right and buildings; a registered business mortgage over plant and machinery; a pledge of vehicles; assignment of insurance policies to the bank as first beneficiary; assignment of key contracts and receivables (offtake, supply); project accounts held with the lending bank so sales proceeds pass through it; and personal or corporate guarantees from sponsors.

In a syndicate, security is held for all lenders in proportion to their shares under the participation agreement. Insurance follows the stages of the project: contractor's all risks during construction, then fire, allied perils and machinery breakdown once operating.

regulation.source: Movable Property Security Right Proclamation No. 1147/2019; Insurance Business Proclamation No. 746/2012, art. 48; A typical Ethiopian bank credit manual (2025)
regulation.text: Security interests such as business mortgages are registered on the Ethiopian movable collateral registry. Under the insurance law there is "no premium, no cover", so a typical bank manual requires all mortgaged or pledged property to be insured, policies endorsed to the bank, renewal notices one month before expiry, and the bank to pay an unpaid premium and debit the borrower's loan account.

rows.label: Construction delay and cost overrun
rows.value: Sponsors and contractor: completion guarantee, cost overrun undertaking, fixed-price contract with penalties

rows.label: Early-year cash shortfall
rows.value: Sponsors: DSRA of 6 months' debt service (about Birr 8 to 10 million) before first repayment

rows.label: Wheat supply and price
rows.value: Sponsors and suppliers: supply contracts with price formulas; foreign exchange plan

rows.label: Physical damage
rows.value: Insurer: contractor's all risks, then fire, allied perils and machinery breakdown; bank first beneficiary

rows.label: Sales and diversion of cash
rows.value: Bank control: collection account with the bank; covenant to route sales through it

scenario.title: The sponsors push back
scenario.situation: Sebeta's sponsors say they will accept only one of three proposed protections: the cost overrun undertaking, the DSRA, or the wheat supply contracts. The downside analysis showed the main risk is margin, with early DSCR of 0.68 and 0.75.
scenario.question: If the bank could keep only one, which ranking logic is soundest?
options: Keep whichever the sponsors like least
Recognize that all three are usually ranked high (overrun undertaking, DSRA, supply contracts) and refuse to drop the protections that cover the biggest risks; negotiate rather than accept one
Accept none; the collateral is enough
Keep only the insurance assignment
scenario.explain: These three protections are normally ranked as the most important. A committee should not trade away cover for the project's largest risks; it negotiates or reduces the loan instead.

lessons.title: Case study: syndicating the Ambo Cement plant
body: A cement plant costs Birr 3,000 million and sponsors offer 35% equity. Our bank's total capital is Birr 4,000 million; the board's appetite for any single project is 15% of capital. Debt is to be repaid over 10 years: 2 years of grace, then 8 equal annual principal payments, at 15%.
The large-exposure limit sets a legal ceiling, but the board's lower appetite sets the practical one. The rest must come from other banks, with a participation agreement that protects everyone.

worked.title: Ambo Cement syndication arithmetic (Birr million)

rows.label: Remaining for other banks
rows.value: 1,350, for example three banks at 450 each

worked.note: Approval sits with the committee the bank's policy reserves for syndicated loans, typically its highest management credit committee.

example.title: Why the lead takes the largest share
example.text: When Bank A led a Birr 900 million syndication for Dire Dawa Textiles PLC, it kept Birr 300 million, the largest single share. Participants Getachew Alemayehu and Rahel Desta, credit heads at two other banks, said they joined because the lead had "skin in the game" and committed to quarterly site visit reports.

scenario.title: How much should we take?
scenario.situation: For Ambo Cement, the relationship manager proposes taking Birr 1,000 million, "the full legal limit", to earn more fees. The board's single-project appetite is 15% of capital (Birr 600 million).
scenario.question: What should the credit analyst recommend?
options: Take Birr 600 million and syndicate Birr 1,350 million to other banks
Take Birr 1,000 million, since it is within the 25% limit
Take the whole Birr 1,950 million and sell down later
Decline because the project is too big
scenario.explain: The board's appetite is binding internally even though the law allows more. Taking more than 25% of capital would also breach the large-exposure directive.

takeaways: Syndicate when a project exceeds the large-exposure ceiling (25% of total capital under SBB/87/2024) or the board's lower appetite.
Participants insist on contract review, independent analysis, inspection rights and regular reports; amendments need the consent of all lenders.
Sponsor support (completion, overrun and shortfall undertakings) keeps construction and early risk with sponsors.
A DSRA, often six months of debt service, is funded before the first repayment and drawn only when cash flow falls short.
The security package covers land and buildings, registered business mortgage, insurance assignment, key contracts and a collection account; in a syndicate it is shared pro rata.

quiz.q: Under a typical Ethiopian bank manual, who approves syndicated loans?
options: Any branch manager
The borrower's board
The lead bank alone
The bank's highest management credit committee
quiz.explain: Syndicated loans are reserved for the top management credit committee.

quiz.q: Which right should a participant bank insist on?
options: To set the borrower's dividend policy
To be repaid before all other lenders
To review the loan contract, do its own analysis, inspect administration and receive regular reports
To change repayment terms alone
quiz.explain: These rights let a participant control the risk it carries.

quiz.q: What is a DSRA and when is it used?
options: A blocked reserve, often 6 months of debt service, drawn only when operating cash cannot meet debt service
A sales account used for daily operations
An account for paying dividends
A fee paid to the lead bank
quiz.explain: It bridges temporary shortfalls such as Sebeta's early years.

quiz.q: Which is a form of sponsor support?
options: Contractor's all risks insurance
A cost overrun undertaking
A mortgage on the land lease
The participation agreement
quiz.explain: Completion guarantees, overrun and shortfall undertakings and interest deposits are sponsor support.

quiz.q: Why should sales proceeds pass through an account with the lending bank?
options: To earn the bank higher fees
Because the law requires all sales in one bank
To monitor sales, control cash and collect instalments before cash can be diverted
To avoid tax
quiz.explain: A collection account gives the bank visibility and control.

quiz.q: Debt of Birr 1,950 million is repaid in 8 equal annual principal payments at 15%. What is debt service in the first repayment year?
options: Birr 536.25 million
Birr 292.5 million
Birr 243.75 million
Birr 975 million
quiz.explain: 243.75 principal plus 292.5 interest = 536.25.

modules.title: Implementation monitoring and troubled projects
modules.summary: Read progress against money spent, catch overruns and delays while they are small, and restructure a troubled project on forward-looking numbers rather than sunk costs.
objectives: State the objectives of follow-up during implementation and after start-up
Compare physical progress with spending and estimate cost at completion
Recognize the warning signs of a troubled project
Design a restructuring package on forward-looking cash flows and route it to the right authority

lessons.title: Follow-up during implementation
body: Follow-up during construction has three objectives: make sure the borrower mobilizes its own finance on schedule, that all funds are used for the approved purpose without waste or diversion, and that physical progress keeps to the implementation schedule so the project finishes on time without overrun.

Good practice is to obtain progress reports at least quarterly, inspect the site, and release each tranche only against verified progress from an independent engineer. The bank's follow-up starts the day after disbursement and continues until the loan is fully repaid.

regulation.source: A typical Ethiopian bank credit manual (2025), post-disbursement follow-up
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual schedules follow-up visits for project term loans upon each phase of disbursement and once a year after disbursement is finalized, with a visit at any time when a warning signal is observed regardless of the loan amount. Its follow-up objectives include detecting deviations from the credit decision and ensuring instalments are recovered on schedule.

items.label: Equity first
items.text: Confirm the sponsors' contribution is in

items.label: Engineer's report
items.text: Physical progress verified independently

items.label: Site visit
items.text: Bank staff see the works and the invoices

items.label: Release tranche
items.text: Paid direct to contractor or supplier where possible

items.label: Report
items.text: Progress, spending and risks to the approving committee

example.title: "Nearly finished"
example.text: When the contractor on Bahir Dar Grain Silos PLC told relationship officer Yonas Tadesse the works were "nearly finished", he asked for three things: the independent engineer's certificate of percentage complete, the cost to date against budget, and the list of outstanding variation claims. The certificate showed 62% complete, not the 90% implied, and the next tranche was held back.

lessons.title: Follow-up after start-up
body: Once the plant runs, follow-up shifts to performance. The bank collects monthly operating data (volume, utilization, prices, costs), periodic financial statements, performance against the appraisal benchmarks, and evidence of payments to the bank and to other banks.

A daily diary of due dates prevents silent lapses: instalments, insurance renewals, revival of registrations, statement submissions and facility renewals. A lapsed insurance policy or an expired registration can leave the bank unsecured on the one day it matters.

example.title: The two-month insurance gap
example.text: At Wolkite Edible Oil PLC, the fire policy over Birr 35 million of machinery lapsed for two months because nobody sent the renewal notice. A small fire in the boiler room happened in the third week. Under "no premium, no cover" the insurer paid nothing. Bank A now runs a diary that sends renewal notices one month before expiry and pays the premium itself, debiting the loan account, if the customer has not.

scenario.title: Utilization below plan
scenario.situation: Eight months after start-up, Gondar Biscuit PLC reports utilization of 48% against an appraisal benchmark of 60%. Instalments are paid on time so far, partly from the sponsor's other business.
scenario.question: What is the best follow-up action?
options: Nothing; instalments are current
Classify the loan as non-performing immediately
Visit the plant, find the cause, update the cash flow forecast and agree corrective actions, and report to the committee
Call the whole loan
scenario.explain: A gap against benchmark is an early warning. Payments funded from outside the project hide the problem; acting early preserves options. Classification follows days past due, so it is not yet non-performing.

lessons.title: Progress against spending
body: The simplest early warning is to compare the percentage of physical completion (from an independent engineer) with the percentage of budget spent. If spending runs ahead of progress, an overrun is coming.
A simple first estimate of the final cost is the cost to date divided by the percentage complete. It is rough, since some items are front-loaded, but it gives the committee an early number to act on.

visual.caption: Sebeta building at month 9: 21.0 / 0.55 = Birr 38.2 million

worked.title: Reading Sebeta's month-9 progress report

rows.label: Building budget spent (budget Birr 30 m): plan / actual
Machinery
rows.value: At the port; customs documents incomplete

worked.note: Spending (70%) runs ahead of progress (55%). Plant start will slip by at least 4 to 6 months. Stop further building tranches until the engineer verifies progress and the claim; call the sponsors' cost overrun undertaking; help clear the machinery; revise the schedule and cash flow; report to the approving committee.

lessons.title: Warning signs in projects
body: Most troubled projects send signals months before the first missed instalment. The analyst's job is to notice them and act while the problem is still small and cheap to fix.

Watch especially for equity that arrives late or is replaced by short-term borrowing, and for sponsors asking to bring forward the working capital disbursement. Both often mean construction money is running out.

items.label: Late equity
items.text: Or replaced by short-term borrowing

items.label: Disputes and claims
items.text: Contractor or supplier disputes, variation claims

items.label: Machinery at the port
items.text: Customs or foreign exchange delays

items.label: Design changes
items.text: Changes in design or capacity

items.label: Key staff missing
items.text: Plant manager or engineers not hired

items.label: Failed trial runs
items.text: Or requests to bring forward working capital

scenario.title: An early request for working capital
scenario.situation: Four months before scheduled completion, the sponsor of Mekelle Tiles PLC asks Bank A to release the Birr 6 million working capital line now, "to buy raw materials while prices are low". The latest engineer's report is two months overdue.
scenario.question: How should the bank respond?
options: Hold the release, obtain an up-to-date engineer's report and cost-to-date figures, and check whether construction funds have run short
Release it; low prices are good business
Release half now and half later
Cancel the whole loan
scenario.explain: A request to bring working capital forward, combined with an overdue progress report, is a classic sign that construction money may be short. Verify before releasing.

lessons.title: Restructuring a troubled project
body: Decide on forward-looking cash flows: money already spent is sunk, because it cannot be recovered whatever the bank decides. Only future cash flows differ between completing, stopping or selling the project.

Options include sponsors funding the overrun under their undertaking, extending grace and tenor, re-sculpting repayments, capitalizing or deferring interest during the delay, additional security, reducing scope, bringing in a new investor, or selling the project. Fresh bank money for a troubled project needs concrete justification and the right committee.

regulation.source: A typical Ethiopian bank credit manual (2025) and NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual allows a long-term loan to go beyond 10 years only if it is rescheduled because of recoverability concerns and the projected cash flow justifies it; any rescheduling must follow the current NBE directives and be approved by the body holding that authority. Rescheduling requests need an application, latest financial statements, credit information, renewed licences and a projected cash flow. Under SBB/90/2024 classification follows days past due, and restructured loans stay under closer regulatory watch.

items.label: Diagnose
items.text: Cause, cost to complete, revised schedule

items.label: Compare options
items.text: Complete, stop or sell, on future cash flows only

items.label: Sponsors first
items.text: Call undertakings; new equity before new bank money

items.label: Restructure
items.text: Grace, tenor, re-sculpting, security, covenants

items.label: Approve and monitor
items.text: Right committee; tighter reporting

example.title: Sunk cost thinking at a hotel project
example.text: At a Birr 120 million hotel in Arba Minch, a committee member argued, "we have already lost money, so we should stop". Analyst Bethlehem Assefa showed that finishing required Birr 18 million more and would let the hotel open and repay, while the half-built shell would fetch well under the Birr 85 million disbursed. The committee approved completion with sponsor equity first.

lessons.title: Case study: Sebeta one year late and over budget
body: At the planned start date the plant is not ready. Final cost will be Birr 10.5 million over budget and production will start one year late. The bank has disbursed Birr 60 million of the Birr 70 million loan, and the sponsors can fund only Birr 5 million of the overrun. On the original appraisal basis, project NPV at 16% falls to -Birr 17.3 million (IRR 12.6%).

The negative NPV does not mean the bank should stop. The original investment is sunk. The question now is whether completing (Birr 10.5 million more, of which Birr 5.5 million unfunded) gives a better recovery than stopping, where the bank would hold a half-finished plant worth far less than Birr 60 million.

worked.title: Sebeta restructuring package (Birr million)

rows.label: Unfunded gap
rows.value: 5.5: more sponsor equity, a new investor, or as a last resort a small top-up with extra security

rows.label: Repayment
rows.value: One more year of grace, re-sculpted schedule, tenor beyond the original end date (a rescheduling decision)

rows.label: Protections
rows.value: Personal guarantees, DSRA before first repayment, tighter reporting

worked.note: Approval by the committee with rescheduling and restructuring authority; classification and provisioning follow NBE rules.

scenario.title: Stop or complete?
scenario.situation: A committee member says: "The re-run NPV is -Birr 17.3 million. The project destroys value. Stop disbursing and foreclose." Birr 60 million is already disbursed and completing needs Birr 10.5 million more.
scenario.question: What is the correct analytical reply?
options: Agree: a negative NPV means stop
Wait a year and decide later
Disburse the full overrun from the bank to avoid embarrassment
The Birr 60 million is sunk; compare future cash flows from completing with the value recovered by stopping. Completion is almost certainly the better recovery
scenario.explain: Restructuring decisions compare only future cash flows. The re-run NPV includes money already spent, which no decision can recover.

takeaways: Implementation follow-up checks that finance is mobilized on schedule, funds go to the approved purpose and progress keeps to schedule.
If spending runs ahead of physical progress, an overrun is coming; estimated cost at completion = cost to date / percent complete.
Late equity, claims, machinery at the port, design changes and early working capital requests are warning signs.
Restructure on forward-looking cash flows; money already spent is sunk.
Sponsors fund first; fresh bank money needs concrete justification and the committee holding rescheduling authority.

quiz.q: Which is an objective of follow-up during implementation?
options: Maximizing fee income
Setting the borrower's selling prices
Ensuring funds are used for the approved purpose without waste or diversion
Choosing the contractor
quiz.explain: The three objectives are finance mobilized on schedule, funds used for the approved purpose, and progress on schedule.

quiz.q: A building is 40% complete with 55% of the budget spent. What does it signal?
options: The project is ahead of schedule
A likely cost overrun: spending is ahead of progress
Nothing; the two figures are unrelated
The contractor should be paid a bonus
quiz.explain: Spending ahead of progress points to an overrun.

quiz.q: Cost to date is Birr 18 million and the work is 60% complete. Estimated cost at completion?
options: Birr 10.8 million
Birr 28.8 million
Birr 45 million
Birr 30 million
quiz.explain: 18 / 0.6 = Birr 30 million.

quiz.q: Why ignore sunk costs in a restructuring decision?
options: They are always small
Accounting rules require it
They cannot be recovered whatever is decided, so only future cash flows differ between options
Sponsors prefer it
quiz.explain: Only future cash flows separate completing, stopping or selling.

quiz.q: Which is a warning sign during construction?
options: Machinery stuck at the port
Equity paid in early
Trial runs passed
Engineer's reports on time
quiz.explain: Port delays, claims, late equity and design changes are warning signs.

quiz.q: Under a typical Ethiopian bank manual, how often are project term loans visited after disbursement is finalized?
options: Never
Once a year, plus at each disbursement phase and whenever a warning sign appears
Every week
Only at maturity
quiz.explain: The visit timetable sets each disbursement phase and once a year after disbursement is complete.

modules.title: Integrated capstone: leading a committee through a complex decision
modules.summary: Bring the course together on one complex, troubled project and defend a recommendation before a credit committee.
objectives: Diagnose whether a project's problem is market, operations, structure or sponsor behavior
Appraise an expansion as a separate project and assess its effect on the group
Set conditions and covenants that protect the bank's existing and new exposure
Apply NBE classification and provisioning rules and name the approving authority
Present and defend a recommendation clearly

lessons.title: Sebeta two years on
body: Sebeta was rescheduled after its one-year delay. It has now operated for two years. Utilization is rising but below the 85% plan, and DSCR was below 1.0 in year 1, drawing on the DSRA.

Other facts complicate the picture: a competitor mill opened 40 km away; the sponsors propose a Birr 25 million pasta line (60% bank financed) to use idle capacity and diversify; the environmental audit found the dust filters not installed; the insurance policy lapsed for two months last year; and a second bank has offered the sponsors a working capital line secured on stock.

worked.title: Sebeta operating results after rescheduling
worked.note: Price is 3.3% below the Birr 6,000 base in year 2, close to the -4.1% switching value. The DSRA did its job in year 1 but now needs topping up.

example.title: Team roles at the mock committee
example.text: Each team splits into an analyst, a risk officer, a legal and security officer and a committee member. In the pilot session, Mulugeta Kassa played the committee chair and opened with one question: "Is this a new loan, or a rescue of the old one dressed up as growth?" The best teams answered it in their first minute.

lessons.title: Diagnosis: market, operations, structure or sponsor?
body: Start by separating the existing loan from the new request. Then diagnose the existing project using the Day 1 switching values: price and variable cost are close to their switching values, so the competitor matters more than the delay. Utilization is improving but still below plan and below cash break-even plus margin.

The structure worked: DSCR under 1.0 in year 1 was covered by the DSRA, exactly as designed. But sponsor behavior raises concerns: dust filters not installed and a two-month insurance lapse are breaches of conditions the bank set.

left.title: Pointing to market risk
items: Price 5,800, close to the -4.1% switching value

right.title: Pointing to sponsor behavior
items: Talks with a second bank for a stock-secured line

scenario.title: What is the main problem?
scenario.situation: Your team must state Sebeta's main problem in one sentence for the committee. DSCR rose from 0.95 to 1.12, the DSRA covered the gap, price is near its switching value and a competitor has opened nearby.
scenario.question: Which diagnosis is best supported by the evidence?
options: Mainly market (margin) risk, aggravated by weak sponsor compliance; the structure itself worked
The structure failed: the DSRA was too small
Pure construction risk from the earlier delay
No problem: DSCR is above 1.0 now
scenario.explain: Price near its switching value and a new competitor point to margin risk; the DSRA performing as designed shows the structure worked; the breaches show sponsor discipline is weak.

lessons.title: Appraising the pasta line separately
body: An expansion must be appraised as a separate project with its own cash flows, NPV and DSCR, so that a weak expansion does not hide behind a strong existing business, or the reverse, and so the new money has its own justification and security. Then assess its effect on group DSCR and risk.

Under a typical Ethiopian bank manual, an expansion counts as a project loan when it increases production capacity by more than 40%, and it needs a feasibility study before the full loan process. A strong recommendation finances the pasta line only after the existing loan shows DSCR of at least 1.20 for two quarters (a typical bank benchmark, not a manual rule), with more than the standard 30% equity because the group is already stretched.

visual.caption: The sponsors' proposal already offers 40% equity; teams test whether it is enough given the stretched group.

worked.title: Pasta line: what the committee needs to see

rows.label: Cost and financing
rows.value: Birr 25 m: Birr 15 m loan (60%), Birr 10 m equity (40%)

rows.label: Stand-alone appraisal
rows.value: Own NPV, IRR and DSCR with its own sensitivities

rows.label: Group test
rows.value: Combined DSCR of existing loan plus new debt in the downside

rows.label: Trigger before new money
rows.value: Existing loan DSCR of at least 1.20 for two quarters

rows.label: Conditions precedent
rows.value: Dust filters installed, insurance restored and endorsed, DSRA topped up

worked.note: If the stand-alone DSCR is weak or the group downside falls below 1.0 with no reserve, the expansion should wait.

lessons.title: Covenants and conditions
body: Conditions protect both the existing loan and any new money. Environmental and insurance breaches become conditions precedent to any new disbursement. The DSRA is restored to its six-month level. Equity for the expansion comes in before the bank's money.

The second bank's stock-secured working capital line threatens our security and our control of cash. It needs either an intercreditor agreement or our consent under the negative pledge, with pari passu treatment where shared security is agreed.

items.label: Equity
items.text: Above the standard 30% for the pasta line, paid in first

items.label: DSRA top-up
items.text: Back to six months of debt service

items.label: Environmental deadline
items.text: Dust filters installed and audited by a date

items.label: Insurance
items.text: Bank as loss payee; renewal diary

items.label: Negative pledge and pari passu
items.text: No security to the second bank without consent

items.label: Reporting
items.text: Monthly operating data, quarterly statements

scenario.title: The second bank's stock line
scenario.situation: The sponsors tell you a second bank will lend Birr 12 million of working capital secured on Sebeta's flour and wheat stock. Your loan agreement contains a negative pledge, and your collection account covenant requires sales to pass through Bank A.
scenario.question: What is the right response?
options: Ignore it; stock is not part of your security
Insist that any such line needs your consent under the negative pledge and an intercreditor agreement covering security ranking and cash flows
Immediately call your loan
Offer to lend the Birr 12 million yourself with no conditions
scenario.explain: A negative pledge exists to stop other lenders taking security that weakens the bank's position. Consent and an intercreditor agreement keep ranking and cash control clear.

lessons.title: Authority, classification and provisioning
body: Classification depends on actual days past due, not on DSCR. Sebeta's instalments have been met, with the DSRA's help, so the loan may still be performing even with a weak DSCR. A loan that has been rescheduled stays under closer watch under NBE rules, and any new rescheduling must follow the current directives.

The approving authority is the committee that holds authority for rescheduling, restructuring and new project loans of this size under the bank's delegation. Project loans of any size are typically decided at head-office level, never at branch or district level.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024 (Asset classification and provisioning)
regulation.text: Loans are classified by days past due, with collateral ignored in classification, and carry minimum provisions: pass 1%; special mention (30 to 89 days past due) 3%; substandard (90 to 179 days) 20%; doubtful (180 to 359 days) 50%; loss (360 days or more) 100%. Interest stops accruing on all non-performing loans, an NPL that is 20% or more of a customer's exposure reclassifies the customer's other loans, and restructured loans of 5% of capital or more are reported quarterly.

items.label: Pass
items.text: Up to 29 days past due: 1% minimum provision

items.label: Special mention
items.text: 30 to 89 days: 3%

items.label: Substandard
items.text: 90 to 179 days: 20%

items.label: Loss
items.text: 360 days or more: 100%

worked.title: Provisioning effect on Sebeta (illustrative, outstanding Birr 66 million)

rows.label: Extra provision if Sebeta slips from pass to substandard

worked.note: Missing payments for 90 days would cost the bank about Birr 12.5 million of extra provision, before any loss. That is why keeping the DSRA funded matters to the bank's own profit.

scenario.title: Classify on DSCR?
scenario.situation: A risk officer proposes classifying Sebeta as substandard because its year 1 DSCR was 0.95. All instalments have been paid on time, partly from the DSRA.
scenario.question: What is correct under NBE rules?
options: Substandard, because DSCR is below 1.0
Loss, because it was rescheduled
Classification follows actual days past due; with no arrears it is not substandard, but it stays under close watch as a rescheduled loan
Classification is left entirely to the analyst's judgment
scenario.explain: SBB/90/2024 bands are based on days past due. A weak DSCR is a monitoring signal, and the rescheduled status calls for closer watch, but it does not by itself set the class.

lessons.title: Presenting to the committee
body: Each team has 8 minutes plus questions. Strong presentations lead with the recommendation, separate the existing loan from the new request, show the numbers that drive the decision, and end with the exact conditions and the approving authority.
Committee members probe the weak points: the switching values, the sponsors' compliance record and the second bank. Answer with numbers and conditions, not reassurance.
points: Open with the recommendation: approve, approve with conditions, or decline
Existing loan: monitor, re-sculpt, add security or classify
New request: stand-alone appraisal and group effect
Conditions: equity, DSRA top-up, environmental deadline, insurance, negative pledge, reporting

example.title: A winning recommendation
example.text: Team Abay, led by Eden Girma, recommended: keep the existing loan performing under close watch and top up the DSRA from the sponsors within 60 days; defer the pasta line until the existing loan shows DSCR of at least 1.20 for two quarters; make dust filters and restored insurance conditions precedent; require an intercreditor agreement before any second bank line; and route the decision to the committee holding restructuring authority. It scored 18 of 20.

takeaways: Separate the existing loan from the new request before anything else.
Use switching values to diagnose: Sebeta's price is near its -4.1% switching value, so the competitor matters most.
Appraise an expansion on its own NPV and DSCR, then test the group; finance it only when the existing loan is stable.
Breaches (environment, insurance) become conditions precedent; a second lender needs consent under the negative pledge and an intercreditor agreement.
Classification follows days past due under SBB/90/2024, not DSCR; rescheduled loans stay under close watch.

quiz.q: What should a strong capstone answer do first?
options: Approve the expansion
Separate the existing loan from the new request
Classify the loan as loss
Ask for a Monte Carlo study
quiz.explain: Mixing the two lets a weak request hide behind the existing business, or the reverse.

quiz.q: Sebeta's year 2 price is Birr 5,800 against a Birr 6,000 base. How far below base is it?
options: About 3.3%
About 1.5%
About 5.8%
About 10%
quiz.explain: 200 / 6,000 = 3.3%, close to the -4.1% switching value.

quiz.q: Under SBB/90/2024, what is the minimum provision for a substandard loan?
quiz.explain: Substandard (90 to 179 days past due) carries 20%.

quiz.q: What does a negative pledge do?
options: Prevents the bank from lending more
Stops the borrower giving security over its assets to other lenders without consent
Reduces the interest rate
Cancels the DSRA
quiz.explain: It protects the bank's security and ranking.

quiz.q: Why are the dust filter and insurance breaches made conditions precedent?
options: They are minor and easy to waive
To increase fees
NBE requires all conditions to be precedent
They show weak sponsor compliance and expose the bank's security and the plant itself
quiz.explain: New money should not flow while existing conditions are broken.

quiz.q: What determines Sebeta's loan classification?
options: Its DSCR
The value of its collateral
Its actual days past due
The sponsors' reputation
quiz.explain: Classification is by days past due; collateral is ignored in classification.

exam.q: Sebeta's base NPV is Birr 19.6 million and falls by Birr 4.8 million for each 1% fall in price. Its contribution margin is 38%. What is the price switching value and what does it imply?
options: About 4.1%; price needs the strongest evidence and contract mitigants
About 38%; price is a minor risk
About 9.4%; construction cost matters more
About 0.8%; the project should be declined
exam.explain: 19.6 / 4.8 = about 4.1%, the smallest switching value, so price is the critical assumption.

exam.q: A project's downside scenario shows DSCR of 0.70 in year 1 recovering to 1.30 by year 3. Which response is soundest?
options: Decline automatically
Shorten the tenor to reduce risk
Approve with no changes because the base case is fine
Approve with a DSRA, a sponsor shortfall undertaking or longer grace in place before the shortfall
exam.explain: A temporary shortfall is covered by cash support; shortening tenor would worsen DSCR.

exam.q: Which statement best distinguishes economic from financial appraisal?
options: Economic appraisal uses market prices and counts taxes as costs
Economic appraisal uses shadow prices, treats taxes and subsidies as transfers and counts external costs and benefits
They are the same analysis with different names
Financial appraisal includes pollution costs; economic appraisal does not
exam.explain: Financial appraisal looks only at the project's own cash.

exam.q: A plant needs 12,000 tonnes of imported wheat at USD 300 a tonne and replaces imported pasta worth USD 5.0 million a year. What is its net foreign exchange saving?
options: USD 1.4 million
USD 3.6 million
USD 5.0 million
USD 8.6 million
exam.explain: 12,000 x 300 = USD 3.6 million spent; 5.0 - 3.6 = USD 1.4 million net saving.

exam.q: Before disbursing to a large project with significant environmental impacts, which set should the bank have?
options: Only the sponsor's assurance
A higher interest rate
EIA approval by the competent authority, costed mitigation measures and a monitoring plan
An export credit guarantee
exam.explain: These belong in the appraisal and as conditions precedent.

exam.q: A sponsor offers duty-free machinery as collateral for a loan to his cousin's separate company. What is the correct treatment?
options: Accept at full invoice value
Do not accept: duty-free assets secure only the privileged owner's own loans in the same sector
Accept at value net of duty
Accept if insured
exam.explain: Duty-free assets cannot be held for third-party loans.

exam.q: Bank A's total capital is Birr 2,400 million and its board appetite for one project is 15% of capital. A project needs Birr 1,200 million of debt. What is the most Bank A should take, and what is left to syndicate?
options: Birr 600 million; Birr 600 million left
Birr 240 million; Birr 960 million left
Birr 1,200 million; nothing left
Birr 360 million; Birr 840 million left

exam.q: In a syndication, which decision requires the consent of all lenders?
options: The lead bank's internal staffing
The agent bank's office location
Rescheduling, extension or other amendment of the loan contract
The participant's own provisioning
exam.explain: Amendments and rescheduling need unanimous consent under the participation agreement.

exam.q: Debt of Birr 800 million is repaid in 8 equal annual principal payments at 16% after 2 years of grace. What is a 6-month DSRA at the first repayment?
options: About Birr 114 million
About Birr 50 million
About Birr 228 million
About Birr 64 million
exam.explain: Principal 100 + interest 128 = 228 a year; half is about 114.

exam.q: Which sponsor instrument places construction cost risk on the sponsors rather than the bank?
options: Assignment of insurance
A cost overrun undertaking
A collection account
A negative pledge
exam.explain: Overruns are funded with sponsor equity, not bank debt.

exam.q: A building is 50% complete, 65% of the budget is spent and cost to date is Birr 26 million. Estimated cost at completion?
options: Birr 40 million
Birr 39 million
Birr 52 million
Birr 33.8 million
exam.explain: 26 / 0.5 = Birr 52 million; spending ahead of progress confirms an overrun.

exam.q: A project has absorbed Birr 90 million; completing needs Birr 15 million more and the re-run NPV on the original basis is negative. What should drive the decision?
options: Comparison of future cash flows and recovery from completing versus stopping or selling
The Birr 90 million already spent
The committee's reputation
The original appraisal's IRR
exam.explain: Money already spent is sunk; only future cash flows differ between options.

exam.q: Which is NOT a standard restructuring option for a delayed project?
options: Extending grace and tenor
Re-sculpting repayments
Bringing in a new investor
Releasing all security to encourage the sponsor
exam.explain: Restructuring usually adds security; releasing it weakens the bank.

exam.q: Under a typical Ethiopian bank manual, when may a long-term project loan run beyond 10 years excluding grace?
options: Whenever the sponsor asks
Only when it is rescheduled because of recoverability concerns and the projected cash flow justifies it
Never, under any circumstances
Only for export projects
exam.explain: Rescheduling beyond 10 years needs cash flow justification and the authorized committee.

exam.q: Why appraise an expansion separately from the existing project?
options: So a weak expansion cannot hide behind a strong business, or the reverse, and new money has its own justification and security
To save time
Because NBE forbids combined models
To raise the interest rate
exam.explain: Then assess its effect on group DSCR and risk.

exam.q: A borrower's loan of Birr 50 million is 120 days past due. What minimum provision applies under SBB/90/2024?
options: Birr 0.5 million
Birr 1.5 million
Birr 10 million
Birr 25 million
exam.explain: 90 to 179 days is substandard at 20%: 0.2 x 50 = Birr 10 million.

exam.q: A borrower with a negative pledge in our agreement gives stock as security to a second bank without consent. What has happened?
options: Nothing; stock is excluded from all agreements
A covenant breach that weakens our security and ranking; it calls for remedy, consent terms or an intercreditor agreement
An automatic upgrade of our security
A change in NBE classification to loss
exam.explain: The negative pledge protects the bank's security and ranking.

exam.q: For a manufacturing expansion to count as a project loan under a typical Ethiopian bank manual, it must increase production capacity by more than:
exam.explain: Renovation or machinery that does not raise installed capacity by more than 40% is not a project loan.

exam.q: Under the large-exposures directive SBB/87/2024, what is the maximum exposure to one counterparty group?
options: 10% of total capital
15% of total capital
25% of total capital
50% of total capital
exam.explain: 10% or more of total capital is a large exposure; 25% is the ceiling.

exam.q: Sebeta's insurance lapsed for two months and a fire occurs during the gap. Which practice would have prevented the loss of cover?
options: A renewal diary with notices one month before expiry, and the bank paying the premium and debiting the loan if the customer does not
Holding a larger DSRA
A negative pledge
Re-sculpting repayments
exam.explain: Under "no premium, no cover" a lapsed policy pays nothing.

sources: Erudite Africa training module: Project Appraisal Level 3: Advanced Project Risk, Structuring and Monitoring (October 2026)
A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), unnamed
NBE directives as listed in the lessons: FXD/01/2024 as amended (including FXD/04/2026), SBB/87/2024, SBB/90/2024

Ethiopian laws: Environmental Impact Assessment Proclamation No. 299/2002, Environmental Pollution Control Proclamation No. 300/2002, Movable Property Security Right Proclamation No. 1147/2019, Insurance Business Proclamation No. 746/2012
